hints: Focus on how properties change as you go down Group 17, chlorine is above bromine so think about size and shielding.
Remember that smaller atoms usually form stronger covalent bonds and hold electrons more tightly, so compare $\text{H-Cl}$ with $\text{H-Br}$ and Cl with Br for ionisation.
Now think about what controls London forces between $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{Br}_2$ molecules, electron number, and decide which element has the weaker intermolecular forces.
walkthrough:
**Place chlorine and bromine in Group 17**

Chlorine is in Period 3 and bromine is in Period 4. Bromine is larger with more shells and more shielding.

Trend rule down the group:
$$\text{atomic radius increases, ionisation energy decreases}$$

**Compare covalent bonds and ionisation**

A smaller chlorine atom overlaps better with hydrogen, so the $\text{H-Cl}$ bond is shorter and stronger than $\text{H-Br}$. Chlorine also holds its outer electron more tightly, so its first ionisation energy is larger than bromine.

$$\text{bond strength: } \text{H-Cl} > \text{H-Br}$$

**Compare silver halide solubility and van der Waals forces**

$\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$ but $\text{AgBr}$ needs concentrated $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$, so solubility is greater for the chloride. For the elements, London forces depend on number of electrons.

$$\text{Cl}_2 \text{ (34e}^-\text{) vs Br}_2 \text{ (70e}^-\text{): Br}_2 \text{ has stronger temporary dipoles}$$

**Pick the property smaller for chlorine**

Bond strength, ionisation energy and silver halide solubility are all larger for chlorine. Only the van der Waals forces between $\text{Cl}_2$ molecules are weaker than between $\text{Br}_2$ molecules, which is why chlorine is a gas and bromine is a liquid.

options.A: Incorrect. The $\text{H-Cl}$ bond is stronger than $\text{H-Br}$ because Cl is smaller, so orbital overlap is better and bond length is shorter. This property is larger for chlorine, not smaller.
options.B: Incorrect. First ionisation energy decreases down the group due to increased distance and shielding. Chlorine holds its 3p electron more strongly than bromine holds its 4p electron, so this is larger for chlorine.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{AgCl}$ is soluble in dilute $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$ while $\text{AgBr}$ is only soluble in concentrated $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$. Solubility is therefore greater for the chloride, a common test to distinguish them.
options.D: Correct. Van der Waals (London) forces increase with more electrons and larger electron clouds. $\text{Br}_2$ has many more electrons than $\text{Cl}_2$, so induced dipole attractions are stronger for bromine and weaker (smaller) for chlorine.
